status.en: 235 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Lagos, Abuja and Kaduna.
status.nb: 235 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Lagos, Abuja og Kaduna.

summary.en: Gunmen killed seven civilians in a Plateau community and shot Islamic cleric Yahaya Masussuka dead in Katsina, while a separate gang attack in Binnari, Taraba left at least 62 dead. Bandits seized logistics supplies in Benue and attempted abductions in Zamfara, where troops rescued two herders and recovered livestock, and in Sokoto where troops foiled a terrorist ambush. Military operations destroyed a bomb-making hideout in Borno, killed 15 terrorists and two ISWAP commanders, and neutralised 44 terrorists in another Borno strike. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Våpenbærende menn drepte syv sivile i et samfunn på Plateau og skjøt den islamske lærde Yahaya Masussuka død i Katsina, mens et separat gjengangrep i Binnari, Taraba etterlot minst 62 døde. Banditter tok logistikkforsyninger i Benue og forsøkte bortføringer i Zamfara, hvor soldater reddet to hyrder og gjenvant husdyr, og i Sokoto hvor soldater avverget et terrorangrep. Militære operasjoner ødela en bombefremstillingshule i Borno, drepte 15 terrorister og to ISWAP-kommandører, og nøytraliserte 44 terrorister i et annet angrep i Borno. Konflikten førte til 1 486 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
